findings.title: Cached peer readiness permits A/G dispatch after an already-observable peer transport failure
findings.confidence: High: reproduced through the real backend and ProcessStream with simulated Docker metadata and real benign local pipes

locations.purpose: Peer admission use checks closed/phase cache, not current transport state
Collection performs slow postflight work after its last current-stream readiness check
A advances the compiled observer toward ptrace SEIZE/INTERRUPT
G advances the target past its admission barrier

findings.root_cause: ProcessStream.closed means that local close() was called, not that its peer pipe remains live. stdout_eof is updated only by pumping. before_input trusts cached peer phase and closed without pumping the peer; _send pumps only the stream being written. collect_native_admission also stores an admission after metadata/attachment/authorization work without a final live-ready check.

observed: After normal target and observer admission, a synchronized Python peer closed stdout, wrote stderr, wrote a partial frame, or wrote an extra complete frame. The fixture confirmed the affected selector was readable before dispatch.
In all four target-peer variants, observer.arm_observer() wrote A and the benign observer recorded it; target remained cached READY/closed=false.
In all four ARMED-observer-peer variants, target.start_target() wrote G and the benign target recorded it; observer remained cached ARMED/closed=false.
EOF introduced during the postflight container-inspection pass still returned phase=native_admission_validated; a subsequent explicit require_admission_ready() rejected the same stream.
No backend admission/private stream fields were forged to obtain these results. The same EOF on the sender stream was rejected as a negative control.

findings.impact: The implemented admission-to-command boundary can arm the scope-owned observer or start the scope-owned target after losing the peer control channel or with already-pending protocol failure. If native feasibility is later established, A is the pre-ptrace release byte. This defeats the claimed lost-peer fail-closed dispatch invariant; an expired/lost external Docker CLI is not itself tracer death, so EXITKILL does not establish safety here.
findings.blast_radius: The current authorized C0 target/observer invocation and integrity of its admission evidence. No arbitrary PID access, host escape, actual ptrace execution, production compromise, or verified failure of the independent watchdog is claimed.
findings.severity_rationale: A concrete safety/admission-gate bypass within an externally authorized, tightly scoped preparation component. No additional OS privilege or cross-scope access was demonstrated.

minimal_fix.description: After the final input-authorizer callback, nonblockingly pump the required peer and reject EOF, stderr, queued/partial output or wrong phase before A/G. Recheck live readiness after all collection postflight work and before recording admission. Preserve existing cleanup/refusal and do not add Docker inspection to HELD/resume.
minimal_fix.code_section: SEC-01: check actual peer transport at the point of use
minimal_fix.core_code:
def require_quiet_live(self, expected_phase):
    require(expected_phase in ('READY', 'ADMISSION_READY', 'ARMED'), 'NATIVE_ADMISSION_TRANSPORT')
    require(not self.closed and self.phase == expected_phase, 'NATIVE_ADMISSION_TRANSPORT')
    self._pump(0)
    require(not self.stdout_eof and not self.frames and not self.decoder.partial, 'NATIVE_ADMISSION_TRANSPORT')
minimal_fix.regression_acceptance: All eight A/G peer-fault variants must refuse with zero command bytes; the postflight EOF case must not return admission. Preserve the live positive control.

findings.title: Final authorization latency bypasses own and peer admission expiry checks
findings.confidence: High: reproduced with real monotonic time and a trusted callback that returns True after bounded latency

locations.purpose: Own/peer expiry checks precede the last authorizer call
No deadline recheck after callback/output pump immediately before write
Admission records retain the deadline end as their expiry

findings.root_cause: before_input checks admitted and peer expires_at, then invokes the final potentially slow authorizer. _send checked its deadline before calling before_input and writes without a post-callback deadline check. A True callback result does not renew the independent admission evidence window.

observed: With ordinary 1.5-second deadlines and admitted live peers, the final actor_input authorization callback slept until 30ms past the recorded deadline and returned True. A was received 34.97ms after expiry; G was received 34.49ms after expiry.

With independently constructed target and observer deadlines, A was also received 30.46ms after the target peer expired while the observer sender still had approximately 4.5 seconds remaining. An own-stream-only deadline fix is insufficient.

The probes used time.monotonic, did not change bound Deadline objects or admission records, and did not revoke approval. Already-expired entry and a final callback returning False both rejected in negative controls.

findings.impact: Commands cross the pre-arm/pre-start boundary using admission evidence outside its independently bounded lifetime. A slow but valid trusted authorization service is sufficient; a malicious controller is not required. The native ten-second control wait is a separate ceiling and does not enforce shorter controller/peer admission expiries.
findings.blast_radius: The current C0 invocation's admission freshness and dispatch safety, not arbitrary execution authority or expanded privileges.
findings.severity_rationale: Deterministic stale-evidence dispatch under plausible callback latency, limited by the scoped actor protocol and independent native/controller ceilings.

minimal_fix.description: Recheck both immutable own and peer admission expiries after the last authorizer callback and peer polling; also check the stream deadline after the callback/pump immediately before each os.write. Do not extend the evidence window to accommodate callback latency.
minimal_fix.code_section: SEC-02: enforce expiry after slow work, directly before write
minimal_fix.core_code:
# After the last authorization callback and peer polling:
require(deadline.clock() < admitted['expires_at'], 'NATIVE_ADMISSION_EXPIRED')
require(peer['stream'].deadline.clock() < peer['expires_at'], 'NATIVE_ADMISSION_EXPIRED')
# In ProcessStream._send after callback and output pumping, before os.write:
self.deadline.check()
minimal_fix.regression_acceptance: Slow-True-authorizer tests for A, G and peer-only expiry must refuse and emit zero bytes; retain explicit-revocation, already-expired and live-positive controls.

checks.name: Static boundary review
checks.actual: Traced native collectors and A/G barriers, Python exact schemas/context/peer revalidation, owned metadata/attachments/generation checks, stream ordering, authorizers, deadline use, policy generation and cleanup separation. The two findings are in implemented dispatch/collection paths, not deferred workers.
positive_observations: Raw validation requires exact canonical bounded JSON, nonzero lowercase 64-hex identities, exact integers rather than bool coercions, singleton tasks/processes, zero capabilities, UID/GID 999, fixed resource ceilings and externally supplied context.
Observer validation revalidates original target frames; summaries retain execution_authorized=false and runtime_evidence=false.
Generation anchoring before case dispatch and metadata comparisons during collection reject the tested precollection PID/start change and image substitution.
Native observer source waits for A before PTRACE_SEIZE; target source waits for G. No caller PID/address selectors or privileged fallback were introduced in the inspected paths.
Local CLI closure is not promoted to remote absence. Existing independent watchdog/ownership cleanup contracts remain separate.

checks.name: Existing offline suite
checks.note: Offline contract/metadata tests and benign Python process fixtures only. Not 99 native experiments.

checks.name: Independently authored offline security probes
checks.actual: 24 strict frame mutations and 9 malformed wire inputs rejected; case/nonce/peer receipt replay controls, default deny, missing admission, generation/image substitution, sender EOF, revocation, already-expired and live-positive controls exercised. Nine SEC-01 variants and three SEC-02 variants reproduced. Tests for findings deliberately assert the vulnerable behavior; green probe output is not a security clearance.
retained_attempts: offline-probes.log/json: initial 14-test attempt had two harness/cleanup errors; peer-gate reproductions already succeeded. One input-log existence/read race was corrected in the private probe only; Darwin LOCAL_PROCESS_CLEANUP was handled only after confirming the child was reaped and every pipe closed. No application error was silently converted to an acceptance result.
offline-probes-final.log/json: 16-test rerun passed and reproduced both findings.

offline-probes-confirmation.log/json: 17-test final run passed, adding the separate peer-expiry case. Per-fixture config, received-input, fault-trigger and metadata/authorization logs remain under security/tmp/.

checks.name: Static ELF, compiled BPF, profile and format-template checks
checks.actual: Two AArch64 ET_DYN ELFs have no PT_INTERP, no writable-executable load segment, non-executable GNU_STACK and GNU_RELRO. Five target manifest symbol/instruction joins matched. Observer .obs_filter bytes match the retained BPF and deterministic generator; independent BPF interpretation passed 4680 bounded architecture/syscall/request/TID/regset cases, including high-bit aliases and exec denial. All three retained OCI profiles exactly match current generation and default-deny policy. PRCTL allowlists are target [3,21,39], observer [3,21,22,39], oracle [39]; observer 22 remains the reviewed filter installer. Eight extracted format strings were rendered into 16 independent Python-frame joins, including the longest native case; largest frame for these independently chosen values was 662 bytes, below 1024.
checks.note: Wire-template matching and BPF interpretation are static/simulated checks, not collector execution or installed-kernel-filter readback.

checks.name: Scoped secrets scan and checksum classification
checks.actual: Pinned Gitleaks dir scan returned 0 and []; explicit embedded-default config, empty ignore, --ignore-gitleaks-allow, --max-decode-depth 2, redacted output. No custom suppression. Independent literal search found only two occurrences of the GCC FROM manifest checksum, classified as a non-credential image digest; no inline allow comments found.

checks.name: Targeted authoritative research
checks.actual: Consulted Linux pipe EOF/nonblocking semantics, PID-namespace init termination and ptrace EXITKILL semantics to distinguish local transport loss from tracer death and remote cleanup. No private source or workspace data was supplied to web research.

source_preservation.actual: Exact same full source/artifact file inventories, SHA256 hashes, sizes and recorded descendant file/directory modes. No source additions, modifications or deletions; no snapshot permission mutation. Base archive and intake unchanged.

limits: No target or observer execution, including --help; no ptrace, native experiment, Docker invocation/build/mutation, Redis process/network experiment, or production access.
No commits, pushes, PRs, shared-original/worktree changes, source permission changes or further delegation.
Synthetic metadata and real local Python pipes establish Python boundary behavior only; they do not prove Linux/Docker Desktop admission feasibility or actual native ptrace effects.
The trusted context producer, oracle/client-closure worker, runtime images, full evidence/approval assembly and all deferred experiments were not counted as bugs.
Static artifact analysis does not constitute a full compiler/libc/OpenSSL CVE audit, binary equivalence proof, runtime seccomp bytecode readback, or whole-trial confinement/resource proof.
Remediation code is supplied for implementation by the owner; no application changes or remediation retest were performed.
No finite static/probe review proves the absence of all security defects. Nonblocking liveness checks can reject already-observable loss but cannot guarantee future channel lifetime atomically.
